parties.counterparty: SFG Financial Corp, a/k/a E-Path FX (Licensor/Vendor)

plans.note: Liability caps/exclusions in this form typically sit immediately after the warranty disclaimer (Article VIX and the all-caps blocks) or in the general provisions; check for a one-sided cap benefiting Licensor and absence of carve-outs for confidentiality, IP infringement and willful misconduct.

Look for Licensor IP-infringement indemnity in the later articles (X, XXIV) or general provisions; if only a Licensee-side indemnity exists, treat as deviation, and if no indemnity appears anywhere, mark missing.

Article II 'License Grant and Restrictions' and the Confidential Information/Non-Solicitation article are the likely homes for any restriction on the businesses we may operate or competing platforms we may license or build.

'Right of First Refusal' is a defined term, so an exclusivity-style constraint is likely defined in Article I and operative in Article II or the commercial article VIII; assess whether it locks us to Licensor for future FX platform needs.

No MFN language signalled; check the tiered per-trade pricing schedule and the Right of First Refusal definition for any obligation on us to extend best terms to Licensor before concluding absent. An MFN in our favour would not be flagged.
Article X / 'CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION/NON SOLICITATION' is the direct hit; test duration, whether it binds only Licensee (mutuality), scope of covered personnel and any general-advertising carve-out.

'Initial Period' is defined in Article I; the term/termination mechanics should sit in one of the later articles (X or XXIV) or general provisions. Confirm whether we may exit on notice without penalty and whether Licensor has a broader walk-away right.

Check the Initial Period definition and the term article for automatic renewal, the non-renewal notice window and any uncapped price uplift on renewal; a missing uplift cap is a rationale note, not a deviation.
Governing law, venue and any arbitration clause will be in the General Provisions block (Article XXIV). New York is likely and acceptable; flag only foreign law or mandatory offshore arbitration.
Assignment/successors language belongs to the General Provisions; verify we may assign to affiliates and to a successor by merger, and that Licensor cannot terminate on our change of control.

Definitions of Licensed Technology, Derivative Work, Moral Rights and Intellectual Property Rights plus the Article II grant/restrictions govern ownership; check for any assignment to Licensor of our data, feedback, configurations or derivative works.
Article II is the grant clause; test whether it extends to our Affiliates (defined) and contractors, the Field of Use limits, and whether the grant is revocable at Licensor's discretion.

Per-trade tiered pricing usually carries a records/verification right; look in Article II restrictions and the fee article VIII for audit frequency, notice, location and who bears cost. Mark missing only if no verification right appears.
Watch for shortfall/true-up charges tied to the Market Day and Supplemental Payments definitions or late-payment penalties in the fee article; service credits running to us are not flagged.

Article VIX is a full warranty disclaimer (as-is, no merchantability/fitness, no assurance defects will be corrected); assess against the rule as a likely deviation for absence of any affirmative performance warranty or repair remedy.
No insurance heading in the outline; sweep the General Provisions before marking missing, given Licensor hosts the Platform and touches our trade data.

The volume-tiered US$ per-unit table plus 'Market Day' and 'Supplemental Payments' definitions may create an effective minimum or take-or-pay; confirm whether any monthly minimum exists and whether we have an exit.

Check the termination-effects language and the confidentiality article (return/destruction of materials) for any data return or wind-down assistance; if only Licensor-favouring return of Licensed Software appears, our data-return and migration help is missing.
